known_conditions below is EMPTY as a pre-implementation placeholder, NOT as a claim that the baseline carries none. The implementing node MUST re-derive it via pnpm ops:test-diff against its own HEAD before committing, per the schema's own instruction that known conditions are verified by machine and never re-adjudicated by prose.

postgres_requirements.rationale: Eleven RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS and six NO_SUPERADMIN_BYPASS_CONTROLS are properties of POLICY EVALUATION, not of SQL text. Grepping a migration for the absence of current_user_is_super_admin proves the string is absent; it does NOT prove that a super_admin principal cannot read a row, that a DECIDED row rejects UPDATE, that UPDATE/DELETE denial-by-omission actually denies, that a no-organization principal sees zero rows rather than all rows, or that FORCE RLS applies to the table owner. Those require a real PostgreSQL instance with real roles, via pnpm db:audit:disposable against the disposable harness — never staging, never production, never the canonical local stack.

sentinels.purpose: A fictional, unmistakable decision-rationale string planted as the decision_rationale of a divergent decision. Its appearance anywhere in audit_logs.before_json or audit_logs.after_json proves the NSB-04 payload contract was violated and that tenant decision content became readable through a relation whose SELECT policy carries the platform-superadmin bypass. Never a real credential and never real tenant text.
A fictional governed-N/A rationale string, planted the same way, proving na_rationale text likewise never reaches an audit payload.

positive_controls.description: EV-01 arithmetic: an evaluation whose criteria mix SCORED and governed NOT_APPLICABLE responses yields a Score in which every NOT_APPLICABLE criterion is absent from BOTH numerator and denominator. Proven by a fixture where excluding-from-both, excluding-from-numerator-only, and scoring-N/A-as-zero each produce a DIFFERENT number, so the test distinguishes the ratified rule from the two plausible wrong ones.

Determinism: the scoring function called twice with identical (criteria, responses) returns byte-identical results, and its module imports nothing from db, no fetch, no Date, no Math.random and no process.env — asserted structurally over the module source, not only behaviourally.

DecisionPolicy totality: for a published policy, every representable COMPUTED score — including each band boundary value from both sides — maps to exactly one member of ('approve','approve_with_conditions','reject'). No score yields zero outcomes and none yields two.

Default designated decider: an evaluation created with no explicit designated_decision_role carries 'organization_admin', and an actor whose role in THAT organization is organization_admin completes T5 successfully (CS-05).

Designated impact_manager: an evaluation explicitly designated to impact_manager is decidable by an impact_manager of that organization, proving CS-06 admits the second member and that the set is genuinely two-element rather than organization_admin plus a comment.

Snapshot atomicity: a successful T5 writes all nine snapshot values — score_snapshot, score_status_snapshot, recommendation_snapshot, decision_policy_hash_snapshot, decision_outcome, decision_rationale (where applicable), decided_by, decided_by_role, decided_at — in the same transaction as the state change, and the audit row for evaluation.decision_recorded exists in that same transaction. A partial snapshot is asserted to be absent, not merely unobserved.

Snapshot is read, not recomputed: after a decision is recorded, publishing a NEW template version with a different DecisionPolicy leaves the decided evaluation's rendered recommendation and derived divergence UNCHANGED, because both come from recommendation_snapshot. This is the control that would catch a read path that recomputes the recommendation from the current template.

Archive from every pre-DECIDED state: T6 (from DRAFT), T7 (from IN_PROGRESS) and T8 (from READY_FOR_DECISION) each succeed and each emit evaluation.archived. All three are exercised — proving ARCHIVED is reachable from the whole pre-decision region, not just from DRAFT.

Template version identity and pinning: (template_id, version) and (template_id, ordinal) are unique; definition_hash and decision_policy_hash are computed server-side over a canonical serialization and are stable across recomputation; and an evaluation that pinned version N is unaffected in every observable way by the publication of version N+1.

Stella-independence (SB-07): with the Stella provider unreachable, disabled and unconfigured in three separate arrangements, every transition T1 through T8 still completes. Evaluate is proven functional without AI rather than merely believed to be.

negative_controls.description: super_admin is REFUSED as a decider at two layers: canDecideEvaluation('super_admin') returns false, and a T5 attempt by a super_admin principal against an organization_admin-designated evaluation is refused server-side and audited as evaluation.decision_refused. This is the single most important control in the manifest — it is the exact violation the hierarchy shorthand would introduce invisibly (CS-07, CS-08, NSB-01).

Zero denominator: an evaluation in which EVERY criterion of the pinned template version is governed NOT_APPLICABLE yields score_status 'SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE', produces NO system recommendation at all (not a defaulted one), and REFUSES T5. The refusal is audited. Additionally asserts the returned score is neither 0, nor -1, nor null-coerced, nor NaN, nor Infinity (ZD-03).

No standing platform-superadmin bypass: the Evaluate migration contains zero occurrences of current_user_is_super_admin, AND — proven against real PostgreSQL — a super_admin principal with no membership in the target organization reads ZERO rows from every Evaluate relation. Additionally asserts no Evaluate content row exists in domain_object_versions, so DRR-01's refusal is enforced and not merely documented.

Audit payload contract: after a divergent decision whose decision_rationale is EVAL-RATIONALE-CANARY and whose governed-N/A rationale is EVAL-NA-RATIONALE-CANARY, neither sentinel appears anywhere in audit_logs.before_json or audit_logs.after_json, while the audit row still carries enough prior state to reconstruct the transition (satisfying the fail-closed logger's FIBC-040 contract). Proves NSB-04 and its reconciliation together, not one at the other's expense.

Divergence rationale is mandatory: a T5 attempt whose decision_outcome differs from recommendation_snapshot and whose decision_rationale is missing, null, empty or whitespace-only is REFUSED server-side; and the same row is UNREPRESENTABLE at the database, proven by a direct INSERT/UPDATE bypassing the action being rejected by the CHECK constraint (CS-09, DIV-03).

No override path (NSB-05): an actor whose role is in EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES but does NOT match the evaluation's designated_decision_role is REFUSED at T5. Additionally, a repository-wide assertion proves no exported action, route handler, script or database function outside the single authorized decision path writes decision_outcome, decided_by or decided_at — the control that proves an ABSENCE rather than testing a presence.

UNANSWERED is not governed N/A: an evaluation with at least one criterion carrying NO response row is REFUSED at T3, and its criteria are NOT excluded from the denominator. Proven against the adjacent case — the same criterion with an explicit NOT_APPLICABLE plus rationale — which DOES pass T3 and IS excluded, so the two cases are demonstrably distinguished (R-07).

Narrow FIB run-review preserved (CS-19): no Evaluate module imports from or writes to lib/pipeline/methodology-review.ts, lib/pipeline/sroi-results.ts or the sroi_run_reviews relation; assertRunMethodologyApprovalAllowed, isInReviewSet and canApproveRunMethodology are byte-unchanged; and the existing methodology-review test suite is green. Proves Evaluate did not annex FIBIU-20's surface.

The other three forbidden roles: analyst, reviewer and viewer are each REFUSED at T5, individually and explicitly. Enumerated separately from N-01 because a hierarchy-threshold implementation would refuse these three correctly while admitting super_admin — so a test that only checks 'low roles are denied' would pass on the broken implementation.

DECIDED is terminal and immutable: T5-then-archive is REFUSED (CS-10), every other transition out of DECIDED is REFUSED, and — proven against real PostgreSQL — an UPDATE against a DECIDED row and a DELETE against any evaluation row are both denied by RLS even for a member of the owning organization.

Tenant isolation by predicate: a principal who is a member of organization B reads ZERO Evaluate rows belonging to organization A; and a principal resolving to NO organization reads ZERO rows rather than ALL rows. The second half is the important one — an ambient or null scope has previously resolved to GLOBAL rather than to refusal in this repository (RLS-10).

Template version immutability: UPDATE and DELETE against a published evaluation_template_versions row are denied by policy omission AND independently rejected by the uellix_forbid_mutation trigger. Both layers are asserted separately, so removing either one is visible (RLS-04). Also asserts a template version with zero criteria cannot be published (ZD-06).

mutation_controls.description: Replace the set-inclusion predicate with the hierarchy shorthand — canDecideEvaluation(role) = hasRole(role, 'organization_admin') — and N-01 MUST turn RED while N-09 stays green. This mutation is the precise real-world hazard (7 existing helpers in lib/auth/permissions.ts use that exact shape), and the asymmetry is the proof: a suite that goes fully green under it is only testing that low roles are denied. This mutation STRENGTHENS the implementation's apparent permissiveness rather than weakening a test, so it is a valid mutation control.

Add OR current_user_is_super_admin() to the Evaluate SELECT policy and N-03 MUST turn RED at BOTH of its halves — the text assertion and the real-PostgreSQL read. If only the text half goes red, the RLS probe is not actually exercising a super_admin principal and N-03 is half-vacuous.

Make the scoring function return 0 with score_status 'COMPUTED' when the denominator is zero, and N-02 MUST turn RED. If N-02 stays green, it is asserting on the status field alone and would not catch a sentinel number reaching the DecisionPolicy bands (R-04).

Add a second write path to decision_outcome — an admin action, a script, or a direct repository helper — and N-06 MUST turn RED. If it stays green, N-06 is testing the authorized path rather than proving the absence of others, and NSB-05 is unproven.

Add an UPDATE policy permitting a snapshot column to be changed on a DECIDED row, and BOTH P-06 and N-10 MUST turn RED. Separately: mutate a stored snapshot value out-of-band and assert that the snapshot-versus-recomputation comparison detects it, which is the control that gives the deliberate score redundancy its purpose.

Add a stored divergence boolean column and switch the read model to read it instead of deriving, then set it to disagree with the two snapshots — P-07 MUST turn RED. This proves the derivation is genuinely a derivation and that no consumer reads a cached divergence (DIV-02, R-05).

Drop the requirement that response_kind = 'NOT_APPLICABLE' carries a non-empty na_rationale and a real recorded_by, and P-01 MUST turn RED — because a governed N/A without rationale and provenance is not a governed N/A under EV-01, and must not be granted the numerator-and-denominator exclusion.

Remove the equality check between the actor's role and designated_decision_role, keeping only set membership, and N-06's first half MUST turn RED while P-04 and P-05 stay green. Green-on-both would mean the designation is decorative and any member of the two-element set can decide any evaluation.
